feed.title: We made the bitcoin-dev mailing list readable: 15 years, 24,699 messages

entry.title: We made the bitcoin-dev mailing list readable: 15 years, 24,699 messages
entry.summary:
A new readable mirror of the bitcoin-dev archive has been established, which is refreshed daily to ensure up-to-date content. Unlike public-inbox, this mirror introduces several enhancements: each discussion thread is presented on a dedicated page with quoted text folded for clarity, and messages are accessible via stable permalinks based on Message-ID. The archive also features three distinct indexes generated from the same dataset—chronological topic timelines, individual pages for every BIP (Bitcoin Improvement Proposal) discussed, and dedicated pages for each author. This organization provides comprehensive navigation and detailed access to the development discussions.
All archived messages are preserved in their original form, ensuring complete fidelity to the source material. The only editorial additions are succinct topic blurbs to aid reader orientation. Each message includes a link to its initial location, maintaining transparency and traceability throughout the archive.
Two specific aspects are highlighted for community feedback. First, the process of name merging consolidates multiple spellings or variations associated with a single email address into one author page—such as combining “Luke-Jr” and “Luke Dashjr”—while deliberately excluding merges across mailing list or group addresses. Corrections or preferences regarding these author pages can be requested at any time. Second, message threading is managed by prioritizing reference headers; where these are absent, subject line matching within a 180-day window is used to associate replies with their threads. Any errors in thread organization can be promptly fixed upon notification.
The creators express an openness to being included among the official [public archives of the list](https://www.openai.com), while also respecting any requests for exclusion. This resource aims to enhance accessibility and utility for those following bitcoin-dev discussions, and feedback is actively encouraged to improve its accuracy and usefulness.
